title: Hybrid Identity Configuration
scenario: NewVue Health is integrating its on-premises Active Directory environment with Microsoft Entra ID so that users can be synchronized between the local domain and the cloud tenant. The organization will use Azure AD Connect to establish this relationship before moving to later phases of hybrid identity and device registration. Because this is a complementary activity, use the case study and reference information below to complete the required tasks.

activities.title: Task 1 - Establish Hybrid Identity
activities.prompt:
Drag and Drop Task
You want to establish hybrid identity between the on-premises directory and the cloud tenant.
To answer, move the appropriate actions from the list of actions to the answer area and arrange them in the correct order.
steps: Sign in with the cloud global administrator account
Provide the on-premises Active Directory credentials
answer: Sign in with the cloud global administrator account
Provide the on-premises Active Directory credentials
activities.explanation: Hybrid identity setup requires the synchronization tool, cloud credentials, local directory credentials, configuration choices, and final synchronization.

activities.title: Task 2 - Identify Component Roles
activities.prompt:
Matching Task
You want to explain the role of each hybrid identity component.
To answer, match each component on the left with its function on the right.
activities.explanation: Hybrid identity depends on understanding the roles of the cloud identity plane, the local directory, and the synchronization engine.

activities.title: Task 3 - Select the Sign-In Method
activities.prompt:
Dropdown Task
You want to keep the hybrid deployment simple while allowing passwords from on-premises users to be used in the cloud.
To answer, select the sign-in method that best supports that objective.
activities.explanation: Password Hash Synchronization is the common streamlined sign-in method for basic hybrid identity deployments.

activities.title: Task 4 - Limit Synchronization Scope
activities.prompt:
Dropdown Task
You want to reduce unnecessary cloud objects and synchronize only the required identities.
To answer, select the configuration choice that best supports that objective.
options: Select the required organizational units for synchronization
Synchronize every local object without filtering
activities.answer: Select the required organizational units for synchronization
activities.explanation: Scoped synchronization limits cloud object creation to the required directory containers.

activities.title: Task 5 - Validate Synchronization
activities.prompt:
Drag and Drop Task
You want to verify that synchronization was configured successfully.
To answer, move the appropriate validation actions from the list of actions to the answer area and arrange them in the correct order.
steps: Complete the Azure AD Connect configuration
answer: Complete the Azure AD Connect configuration
activities.explanation: Validation occurs after synchronization completes and the synchronized objects can be reviewed in the cloud.

activities.title: Task 6 - Complete the Synchronization Command
activities.prompt:
PowerShell Task
You want to trigger synchronization from the Azure AD Connect server.
To answer, select the appropriate value for each blank in the command.
activities.explanation: A delta sync is commonly used to trigger synchronization of recent changes.

activities.title: Task 7 - State the Hybrid Objective
activities.prompt:
Dropdown Task
You want users to sign in with identities that originate in the local domain while still being available in the cloud.
To answer, select the statement that best describes the purpose of hybrid identity in this case study.
options: Synchronize on-premises identities to the cloud tenant
Replace the cloud tenant with a local workgroup
activities.answer: Synchronize on-premises identities to the cloud tenant
activities.explanation: The purpose of hybrid identity here is to make local identities available in the cloud environment.
